title: The Compassion of Christ
sourceBasis: World English Bible — 66-book Old and New Testament Scripture text already installed in Iron Sharpener
definition: The compassion of Christ is His merciful and active care toward the weak, suffering, sinful, burdened, and lost. Jesus sees real need and moves toward people with truth, mercy, and help.
summary: The compassion of Christ is His merciful and active care toward the weak, suffering, sinful, burdened, and lost. Jesus sees real need and moves toward people with truth, mercy, and help.
christFocus: Jesus reveals the compassion of God by healing, teaching, welcoming, forgiving, feeding, weeping, and giving Himself for sinners. His compassion is holy love that moves toward the needy.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Jesus’ compassion is not distant pity. He sees the crowds as sheep without a shepherd, touches the unclean, comforts the grieving, feeds the hungry, and calls the weary to Himself.

His compassion is holy. Jesus does not excuse sin or flatter people in brokenness. He brings mercy that heals, truth that corrects, and grace that restores.

The compassion of Christ reaches people others overlook: the sick, ashamed, disabled, demon-oppressed, grieving, poor, sinful, and outcast. He does not treat human need as an interruption to His mission.

The greatest display of His compassion is the cross. He does more than feel for sinners; He gives Himself to save them and open the way for mercy before God.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
Many people believe their weakness makes them unwanted by God. The compassion of Christ answers that lie with the Savior who moves toward the needy and calls the burdened to come.

This doctrine also shapes ministry. A Christ-centered church cannot be cold toward suffering people. Truth and mercy belong together because they are united in Jesus.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Bring your burdens to Christ instead of hiding them in shame. Receive His mercy, submit to His truth, and learn to move toward others with the same compassion He has shown you.
